name: Alex G
label: RCA
lede: A kid from Havertown records in his bedroom, Frank Ocean emails him, and fifteen years later he is on a major label making his warmest record yet.

eras.title: Sandy on Bandcamp
eras.text: A teenager in the Philadelphia suburbs uploads songs recorded alone, and the internet does the rest. Three albums in three years, no label, no band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alex G · Spin: (Sandy) Alex G
years.h: Seventeen, Havertown, a Bandcamp page
years.p: Alexander Giannascoli starts self-releasing albums, EPs and singles as Alex G, recorded at home after Haverford High School.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates his first releases to 2010, when he was 17. Before that came school bands with silly names: MOTHER, a goth-techno project with his sister Rachel, The Scoli Xtreme with his brother, and The Skin Cells, which he has described as pop rock that accidentally ended up punk.

He later explained the "(Sandy)" tag by saying it was the first thing he put on Bandcamp, since the page lived at sandy.bandcamp.com.

years.h: Temple University, English major, briefly
years.p: Giannascoli enrolls at Temple to study English with teaching in mind, then drops out to make records.

years.h: Trick: the dog in the church
years.p: A Bandcamp album with a German Shepherd bolting down the aisle of a Philadelphia church on the cover.
years.xp:
His sister Rachel took the cover photo at their grandmother's funeral at St. Donato Roman Catholic Church in Philadelphia. Giannascoli has said a dog of unknown ownership ran in and out again.

Lucky Number reissued Trick in 2015. In 2022 songs from it, including Sarah and Mary, found a second life on TikTok and Spotify, ten years after he posted it.

eras.title: A label, then a bigger one
eras.text: Orchid Tapes puts out DSU, Europe gets it via Lucky Number, and Domino signs the bedroom guy. He keeps recording the same way.

years.h: DSU on Orchid Tapes: Dream State University
years.p: His label debut runs 32 minutes. The title began as his sister's suggestion of "Dream State," which he inflated into a fake college.
years.xp:
Rachel Giannascoli suggested Dream State after hearing the songs, and he riffed it into Dream State University, a joke on American state schools. He had second thoughts at the last minute; the acronym stuck anyway.

Emily Yacina sings on several tracks. Pitchfork later put DSU at No. 165 on its list of the 200 best albums of the 2010s. Lucky Number issued it in Europe that November with two bonus tracks.

years.cap: Alex G at the Fader Fort, SXSW, Austin, Texas, 2015 · Wikimedia
years.h: Lucky Number brings DSU to Europe, with Rules and Trick in tow
years.p: The London label issues DSU with two bonus tracks and reissues the early Bandcamp albums Rules and Trick, so British fans can finally buy the ones they had been streaming.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the Lucky Number release of DSU, with two bonus tracks, and the Rules and Trick reissues to November 2014. The Trick page lists a Lucky Number mastering date of April 2015, so sources differ.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alex G · Spin: (Sandy) Alex G
years.h: Beach Music: Domino signs the Bandcamp kid
years.p: His first album for Domino Recording Company, an indie label with a rack of Anglo-American stars behind it and no need for him to change his method.
years.xp: Rolling Stone announced the album in August 2015. Spin noted that after six years of uploading self-recordings, this was the leap from Bandcamp to a big indie.

eras.title: Frank Ocean's guitarist
eras.text: The most mysterious man in pop emails a kid from Havertown. Giannascoli plays on Endless and Blonde, tours with Ocean, changes his name in parentheses, and makes Rocket.

years.cap: Alex G at the Fader Fort, SXSW, Austin, Texas, 2015 · Wikimedia
q: He just took the little pieces that worked for him.
years.src: Spin: (Sandy) Alex G · Wikipedia: Alex G · Pitchfork: Alex G Opens Up
years.h: Frank Ocean emails. Guitars end up on Endless and Blonde
years.p: Giannascoli plays guitar and helps with arrangements on both of Frank Ocean's 2016 records.
years.xp:
Spin reports that Ocean contacted him by email. Giannascoli was modest about it: "He just took the little pieces that worked for him." He said he did not want credit for what was Ocean's vision.

Pitchfork ran a 2016 piece in which Giannascoli talked about the sessions. He also joined Ocean's live band on guitar in 2017.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alex G · Spin: (Sandy) Alex G · Stereogum
years.h: Alex G becomes (Sandy) Alex G
years.p: He announces the parenthetical name with no explanation. Spin points to a trademark dispute with a YouTuber named Alex Blue.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Giannascoli said Sandy was the first thing he put on Bandcamp. The parentheses were meant to be silent, but people kept saying it aloud. Spin's 2017 profile says another musician had trademarked "Alex G."

In June 2020 Stereogum reported he had dropped the Sandy for good.

years.h: Rocket: fiddle, banjo and GarageBand
years.p: Molly Germer's violin and John Heywood's bass join a record of Appalachian-leaning songs, with five singles out before release day.
years.xp:
Bobby and Witch dropped March 2, Proud on April 4, Brick and Sportstar on May 4. Metacritic lists it at 82. Spin's profile noted he was still recording largely in GarageBand.

Esquire and Time Out New York both placed it at No. 5 on their year-end lists.

years.h: Molly Germer: partner, violinist, every record since Rocket
years.p: Violinist [[Molly Germer|4ee5bf1c-655f-45f1-a75f-c9539c73f0fc]] has played violin and sung backing vocals on each of his albums since Rocket, and sometimes plays live in the band.

eras.title: Sugar houses and static
eras.text: He drops the parentheses, builds a fairy-tale record around a casino, then goes into real studios with Jacob Portrait. Meanwhile a filmmaker gives him a horror score to write.

years.src: Wikipedia: House of Sugar · Wikipedia: Alex G
years.h: House of Sugar: a casino and a gingerbread house
years.p: The title nods to Philadelphia's SugarHouse casino and to Hansel and Gretel. Pitchfork gave it 8.6 and ranked it No. 17 of 2019.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the name refers both to the then-SugarHouse casino, now Rivers, and to the witch's house in the fairy tale. Four singles came first: Gretel on June 4, Hope on July 15, and Southern Sky and Near in August.

Metacritic scored it 86. Exclaim! gave it 9/10.

years.h: Stereogum: Alex G officially drops the (Sandy)
years.p: Three years after adding it, he takes the parenthetical name out of circulation.

years.h: He co-produces Tomberlin's Projections EP
years.p: A side job while touring is impossible: Giannascoli produces the EP for singer-songwriter Tomberlin.

years.h: He goes to a real studio, and the songs get bigger
years.p: God Save the Animals is his ninth album and the first with producer Jacob Portrait, recorded in Philadelphia, Rhinebeck, Maine, and elsewhere.
years.xp: Seven locations, mostly in the Northeast: Headroom and Spice House in Philadelphia, his home, SugarHouse in New York, Clubhouse in Rhinebeck, Gradwell House in Haddon Heights, NJ, and Watersong in Maine. Portrait, bassist in Unknown Mortal Orchestra, co-produced.

years.h: God Save the Animals: Fallon, Colbert, five stars from NME
years.p: Four singles, TV spots on Fallon (Runner) and Colbert (Miracles), and a Metacritic 86.
years.xp: NME gave it five stars and praised its "newfound clarity and vulnerability". Paste ranked it No. 2 of the year. It was his highest-charting record to that point: No. 144 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Score for We're All Going to the World's Fair
years.p: Director Jane Schoenbrun hires him for the score of her first feature, a film about a teen and an online horror game.

years.h: Trick goes viral ten years late
years.p: Sarah and Mary, posted to Bandcamp in 2012, blow up on TikTok and Spotify.

eras.title: Headlights
eras.text: A major label, Foo Fighters stadiums, a second Schoenbrun film, a Sanders rally, and a record about being a dad.

years.h: Leaves Domino for RCA, and Dave Grohl's stage
years.p: NME reports he has signed with RCA after nine years at Domino and will support Foo Fighters on August stadium dates.
years.xp: Presale for his 2024 US headline tour began January 23, with general sale on January 26, according to NME. On his air of mystery he told the magazine: "I don't feel like I'm that mysterious, I just don't have a lot to say."

years.h: Eight tracks on Halsey's The Great Impersonator
years.p: Giannascoli contributes to eight songs on the pop singer's record.

years.h: Scores I Saw the TV Glow
years.p: Second Schoenbrun film, second score; he would return for Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma in 2026.

years.h: A 30-minute set at Bernie Sanders' Harrisburg rally
years.p: Giannascoli plays the "Fighting Oligarchy" tour stop in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania.

years.h: Afterlife: the first Headlights single
years.p: He announces his tenth album in May and releases Afterlife on May 29, followed by June Guitar and Oranges.

years.src: Wikipedia: Headlights · Albumoftheyear · Pitchfork: The (Real) Alex G · Brooklyn Vegan
years.h: Headlights: 40 minutes of hi-fi dad rock, on RCA
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and ranked it No. 23 of 2025. Co-produced with Jacob Portrait, with Molly Germer on violin.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Ian Cohen called it an upgrade to "hi-fi dad rock" and a major-label debut "worthy of all time indie-graduations". Metacritic lists it at 83 from 15 critics. The Guardian praised a tune built around a pan flute.

Giannascoli played most instruments. String players Carolina Diazgranados, Hannah Nicholas, Carlos Santiago and Justin Yoder added parts. It peaked at No. 166 on the Billboard 200. Albumoftheyear.org lists a separate No. 42 for the year.

years.h: Coachella
years.p: Wikipedia lists Giannascoli among the acts at Coachella in April 2026.
